title: NAT session timeout migration impact assessment
content:
Purpose:
This note documents the planned migration of NAT session timeout defaults and related conntrack/egress controls across private (VPC + on-prem) deployments. It focuses on the networking impact surface (DNS transactions, long-lived websocket/streaming sessions, short-lived HTTP bursts), Terraform changes required, K8s network policy interactions, test plans, rollback criteria, and monitoring runbook entries.

Background / why this matters:
- Symptoms observed: increased 502/504 spikes for streaming inference in certain customers after router upgrades; intermittent DNS failures during bursty startup phases; higher retransmit rates for TCP flows from model-serving pods.
- Root cause hypothesis: default NAT gateway/device conntrack timeouts are too short relative to Redwood workloads (many short-lived ephemeral connections + occasional long-lived streaming). Upgrading NAT behavior without migrating timeouts leads to silent connection drops and TCP/TLS rehandshake costs.

Goals:
1) Reduce customer-facing egress failures by aligning conntrack/timeouts with workload patterns.
2) Make Terraform changes minimally disruptive and reversible.
3) Provide per-customer knobs for strict environments (compliance) vs. relaxed defaults for performance.

Migration surface / scenarios considered:
- Cloud VPC with managed NAT gateway (AWS/NAT GW or GCP Cloud NAT): limited tunability; prefer connection pooling at application/proxy layer.
- Customer-managed NAT VM / HAProxy / on-prem firewall: can tune conntrack, TCP timeout, and UDP tracking.
- Egress via egress-proxy sidecar (envoy) or node-level masquerade: config changes instead of infra changes.

Terraform changes (proposal):
- Module: private-deployments/egress/nat
  - Add variable: nat_conntrack_timeouts = { tcp_established = "12h", tcp_close_wait = "1m", udp_idle = "30s" }
  - Add variable: nat_conntrack_mode = "managed|proxy|inherited"
  - Conditionals: if nat_conntrack_mode == "proxy" set up an autoscaling egress-proxy ASG + route table override; if "managed" apply cloud-nat config (where supported).
- Outputs: reported_conntrack_settings, applied_mode, impacted_subnets
- Rollback: terraform plan will mark changes to nat resources; update strategy uses canary_subnets tag to apply to one AZ first.

Kubernetes interactions and network policies:
- K8s Services that open long-lived streams (inference streaming): annotate pods with "egress.keep-alive: true" so the node egress-proxy can pin flows and keep conntrack entries refreshed.
- NetworkPolicy: no change expected, but explicitly allow healthcheck IPs for egress-proxy probes; add policy debug label to quickly route traffic through diagnostics pod.
- CNI considerations: for Cilium we recommend enabling connection tracking helpers and setting net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established appropriately on nodes via daemonset.

Firewall / security controls impact:
- Session timers affect stateful firewall rules. If we extend timeouts, audit policies should be updated to accept longer-lived conntrack entries.
- For compliance-sensitive customers, expose a per-customer terraform toggle nat_conntrack_mode = "inherited" to keep vendor defaults. Document security review checklist.

Test plan (pre-prod):
1) Canary AZ: apply module to 1 AZ subnet with 5% traffic; monitor 72h.
2) Traffic profile tests: short burst (1000 ephemeral connections/min for 5m), steady streaming (50 long-lived sockets for 6h), mixed startup churn (rolling deploy with cold caches).
3) DNS testcases: repeated SRV/TXT lookups, 500 concurrent stub-resolutions with split-horizon enabled and verify ttl/negative caching behavior.
4) Chaos tests: simulate NAT gateway failover, conntrack table exhaustion and ensure fallback to proxy route.

Metrics to track (SLO/alert thresholds):
- 5xx egress failure rate (per-customer) > baseline + 0.5% -> alert
- TCP retransmit ratio on node egress > 2% sustained over 5m -> alert
- Conntrack table utilization > 70% -> warn; > 90% -> page
- DNS resolution latency (p95) increase > 150ms -> investigate

Gradual rollout strategy:
- Phase 0: dry-run plan + manual review in infra-council
- Phase 1: enable nat_conntrack_mode=proxy in non-prod and validate metrics
- Phase 2: apply to canary subnets (1 AZ) for 72h
- Phase 3: expand to 25% of customer base (by tag: early-access) for 7d
- Phase 4: full rollout with automated checks and auto-rollback on alert triggers

Rollback and mitigation steps:
- Immediate: revert terraform to previous nat_conntrack settings via plan/apply to canary
- Fast mitigation: enable egress-proxy sidecar for impacted customer clusters and route egress through it
- Longer-term: increase conntrack table size (sysctl) on node pool and enable per-namespace egress proxies for heavy-churn tenants

Operational runbook snippets (for on-call):
- Symptom: sudden spike in 502/504 for streaming endpoints
  - Check conntrack table utilization on NAT/edge node (ssh/metrics), check last reloads
  - Query route table: ensure egress routes point to expected NAT/proxy
  - If conntrack exhaustion: temporarily increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on nodes and add iptables-save snapshot, then trigger controlled rollback
- Symptom: DNS NXDOMAIN bursts during deploys
  - Verify resolvers in /etc/resolv.conf and CoreDNS logs; check any split-horizon ACLs; flush DNS caches on egress proxy

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default conservative timeout values (proposal in variables above) — need sign-off from infra security
- Whether to support per-customer conntrack profiles or only global defaults
- Do we allow managed cloud NAT mode to be modified programmatically for all cloud providers or only AWS for initial launch

Action items (owners):
- Samir: prepare terraform PR with variable scaffolding and plan for canary AZ (due 2024-10-02)
- Lena: design egress-proxy sidecar image and healthcheck hooks (due 2024-09-27)
- Diego: add conntrack metrics dashboards and alert rules (due 2024-10-09)
- Priya: write compliance notes for customers that require fixed short timeouts (due 2024-10-05)

Appendix: quick sysctl knobs (for on-prem appliances)
- net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max = 524288
- net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_timeout_established = 43200  # 12 hours
- net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout = 30

Notes: keep this doc as the canonical migration plan for NAT/conntrack tuning. Iterate after the canary and attach measurements to linked_artifacts.
